column1: SECTION D — STUDENT ENGAGEMENT   |   Observe student behaviors, not just teacher actions. Sample at least 5 students across different locations in the classroom.

column3: Less than 25% of students visibly engaged. Collaboration minimal or absent.
column6: More than 75% actively engaged; energy is visible; students initiating. Structured collaboration on synthesis/problem-solving.
column8:
FICO V3 (D1) + TEACH (Time on Task — Student Focus) + OECD (Active Learning) + HOTS Student Engagement ('Students collaborate on tasks requiring synthesis, evaluation')

Why: The most direct measure of whether teaching is reaching students.

column3: Students copying or doing rote recall only. Passively receiving information.
column4: Students completing tasks but without thinking deeply.
column5: Students applying concepts to new problems (Bloom's Apply/Analyze).
column6: Students creating, evaluating, debating — genuine intellectual work. Actively analyse, interpret, and critique content with supporting evidence.
column8:
FICO V3 (D2) + HOTS (Bloom's Taxonomy) + OECD (Cognitive Activation) + HOTS Instructional Strategies ('Students actively analyse, interpret, and critique content')

Why: Being busy ≠ being engaged. HOTS alignment ensures we measure thinking, not just activity.

column3: No peer interaction; silent individual work only.
column4: Students talk but not about content.
column5: Students discuss content in pairs/groups; academic language used.
column6: Students build on each other's ideas; respectful disagreement; peer teaching. Students debate solutions and propose creative alternatives.
column8:
FICO V3 (D3) + OECD (Collaborative Problem Solving) + TEACH (Culture of Learning) + HOTS Student Engagement ('Students explore multiple perspectives or create novel solutions')

Why: Peer interaction is a force multiplier. In 40+ student Pakistani classrooms, peer learning is a necessity.

column3: Students afraid to answer; avoidance behaviors visible.
column4: Students answer only when certain; no risk-taking.
column5: Students attempt challenging tasks; some comfortable with mistakes.
column6: Students volunteer, ask questions, try difficult problems. Mistakes celebrated. Students freely share and debate ideas.
column8:
FICO V3 (D4) + OECD (Supportive Climate) + TEACH (Positive Language) + HOTS Classroom Environment ('Classroom fosters open discussions and critical thinking')

Why: If students won't take risks, higher-order thinking is impossible.

column3: Most students off-task during independent/group work.
column4: Students start on-task but lose focus quickly.
column5: Students sustain focus for most of independent work time.
column6: Students self-regulate; seek help appropriately; persist through difficulty.
column8:
FICO V3 (D5) + TEACH (Time on Task) + OECD (Classroom Management)

Why: Independent work time reveals whether teaching has transferred. Self-regulation is the ultimate goal.

column3: Students don't interact with provided materials.
column4: Materials used passively (watching video, holding textbook).
column5: Students actively use materials to solve problems or practice.
column6: Students use materials creatively; extend beyond prescribed use.
column8:
TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + OECD (Active Learning)

Why: If students aren't actively using materials, the materials aren't working.

column3: Only front-row or high-ability students engaged.
column4: Teacher attempts inclusion but success is limited.
column5: Students across ability levels and genders are participating.
column6: Deliberate inclusion of marginalized students; no one invisible. Gender-equitable participation.
column8:
TEACH (Culture of Learning — Gender) + OECD (Equity) + FICO V3 (C4) + Training Curriculum (Inclusive Education domain)

Why: Pakistan's gender and ability gaps start in the classroom — this is where they end too.
